question: What voltage is needed to drive 2 amperes through a 6 ohm resistor?

citations.title: Ohm's law worked example
citations.excerpt: For an ohmic resistor at fixed temperature, voltage equals current multiplied by resistance: V = I times R. A 6 ohm resistor carrying 2 amperes has a potential difference of 12 volts.
